newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian PM defends departure of bank officials.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian PM defends departure of bank officials.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Tuesday defended his decision to accept the resignations of two senior central bank officials against the advice of the bank's president.

National Bank of Hungary vice presidents Frigyes Harshegyi and Sandor Czirjak resigned last week after an internal report showed a miscalculated options deal done four years ago could cost the bank over $18 million.
"On the basis of what we heard the two vice presidents had to take responsibility and I accepted (their resignations) because I could not do anything else," Horn told reporters.

When the two men submitted their resignation, their boss, NBH President Gyorgy Suranyi, recommended that Horn should insist they keep their jobs because of the good work they had done their appointment in 1991.
But Horn told reporters that although Harshegyi and Czirjak had done good work, this was "a case in which you could not defer responsibility."

The options deal with Creditanstalt Investment Fund in 1992 was for foreign exchange rate guarantees maturing in 1998. The partners shared forint devaluation risks while Creditinstalt did not have to pay an option fee, a decision which the NBH said could cost it more than three billion forints ($18.87 million).
The resignations come hard on the heels of a scandal over payments of millions of dollars by the state privatisation agency APV Rt to a consultant, Marta Tocsik.

That revelation led to the dismissal of the entire APV board and the minister in charge and amalysts have speculated that Harshegyi and Czirjak would have been treated less harshly but for the public pressure on the governemt from the Tocsik case.
